To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
arc magmatism was imposed on an older, backarc basin in the Kisseynew terrane, Trans-Hudson Orogen.
the Kisseynew arc formed in a back-arc environment, and the arc was emplaced onto the older backarc basin.
the Kisseynew magmatic rocks were derived in a subduction zone setting and that the subduction zone was located in a backarc setting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the tectonic history of the Trans-H Hudson orogen, and the role of subduction and collision in the development of continental crust.
the tectonic and geochemical evolution of the Kisseynew and Flin Flon terranes, and how these terranes were affected during the collision of the Rae and Hearnes cratons.
the temporal and spatial evolution of the Kisseynew arc, which was formed in a backarc setting and subsequently collided with the Sask craton, resulting in the formation of the Trans-H Hudson orogen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Trans-Hudson Orogen was formed during a period of arc magmatism and subduction of the Sask craton beneath the Hearne and Flin Flon cratons.
the arc magmatism was related to the subduction of oceanic lithosphere beneath a continental margin.
the Kisseynew arc magmatism occurred within the Trans-H Hudson orogen between 1840 Ma and 1820.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
magmatism in the Kisseynew and adjacent domains was related to subduction of the Archean cratons to the south.
arc magmatism in the Kisseynew terrane was imposed upon the older backarc basin environment, which is consistent with the tectonic model for the Trans-Hudson event.
arc-related magmatism in the Trans-Hudson was imposed on a backarc basin setting, which was the product of earlier collisional events.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Trans-Hudson collisional orogeny was not a simple collision between two continental plates, but rather a complex process involving the subduction of buoyant crust and the interaction of the subducting slab with the overriding plate. © 2018
the Trans-Hudson collisional orogeny was not a single, monolithic, orogen-parallel process, but rather a complex series of events that included subduction of buoyant crust and arc magmatism.

arc magmatism in the Kisseynew and Flin Flon domains was contemporaneous with backarc basin magmatism within the Wollaston domain, and both were contemporaneous with collisional magmatism in central and northern Saskatchewan.
